The test image shows soybean leaves with prominent green-yellow mottling, puckered/wrinkled texture, and the leaves appear thick and distorted. This is a **leaf** image, narrowing to 16 candidate classes.

Key features: mottling pattern, puckered texture, no discrete lesions or spots. Top candidates: Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Downy_mildew, Powdery_Mildew, Cercospora, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the strongest candidate.
Good match - the BPMV reference shows similar green-yellow mottling with puckering. Let me check other candidates.
Downy mildew shows discrete yellow spots, different from the diffuse mottling and puckering in the test image. Let me check more candidates.
Powdery mildew shows white powdery coating - not a match. Let me check more candidates.
SVN virus shows discrete yellow/brown spots along veins - very different from the diffuse mottling in the test image. Let me check more candidates.
Cercospora shows reddish-purple spots and bronze discoloration - not the diffuse mottling pattern in the test image. Let me check Soybean_rust and Bacterial_Pustule.
Soybean rust shows discrete small brown/red spots with pustules - very different from the test image's mottling pattern.
Bacterial pustule shows discrete raised pustules/spots - not matching. Now let me use my final view to see a second BPMV reference to confirm the match.

This second BPMV reference is an excellent match. Both references show the same characteristic pattern seen in the test image:

- **Green-to-yellow mottling (blotchiness)** across the leaf surface
- **Puckered, wrinkled leaf texture** with distortion
- **Younger leaves in upper canopy** most affected
- No discrete spots, pustules, or lesions - just diffuse mosaic mottling

All 7 other classes I checked (Downy mildew, Powdery Mildew, SVN virus, Cercospora, Soybean rust, Bacterial Pustule) showed discrete spots or different symptom patterns that don't match the test image's diffuse mottling and puckering.
